newsitem.title: UK: EMI upbeat on global music industry future.
newsitem.headline: EMI upbeat on global music industry future.

text.p: Britain's EMI Plc, one of the world's five major music companies, said on Tuesday that prospects for the stuttering global music market remained positive over the medium and long-term.

EMI, which demerged from Thorn Plc three months ago, said its profit before tax and exceptional items rose 9.4 percent to 112.5 million pounds ($187.7 million) in the six months to September 30, 1996.
Net interim dividend per share increased by 12.7 percent to 8.0 pence.

"These are excellent interim results from the EMI Group. They have been achieved against a background of variable growth in the major markets and mixed results from our competitors," Chairman Sir Colin Southgate said in a statement.
"The 12.7 percent increase in the interim dividend reflects our confidence in the long-term health of the music industry and EMI's position within it," he added.
"Over the medium and long-term, the prospects for the global music market remain positive." ($1=.5994 Pound)
